title: Avoid redundant quotes around qualified ranges
description:
Fixes #328

Worksheet names are always single quoted in a qualified range (e.g. 'Sheet1'!A1), so cli's weird-name formatting added a redundant outer pair: ''Sheet1'!A1'.

If color is available, don't add quotes.

If color is not available, apply double quotes.

Side effect: changes how names of named ranges appear. I'm OK with that.

title: Add "Supported By Posit" badge to website
description:
## Overview

This PR adds the "Supported by Posit" badge to the website.

## Background

We've recently started adding a "Supported by Posit" badge across all Posit package websites to create a more cohesive brand presence. The badge appears on the far right of the top navigation bar or at the bottom of the hamburger menu. It links to Posit’s main website. @hadley is involved with this initiative.

The following websites already have the "Supported by Posit" badge: [ggplot2](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org), [Great Tables](https://posit-dev.github.io/great-tables/articles/intro.html), [gt](https://gt.rstudio.com), [Plotnine](https://plotnine.org), [Pointblank](https://posit-dev.github.io/pointblank/), [pointblank](https://rstudio.github.io/pointblank/), and [Quarto](https://quarto.org).

See https://posit-dev.github.io/supported-by-posit/ for more information.

## Changes

- Added a line to `_pkgdown.yml` to include the JavaScript file
- Standardized indentation in `_pkgdown.yml`

title: [feat] format numbers and dates (range_format_pattern)
description:
Proposed as fixes #81, partially fixes #179 . 

New `range_format_pattern()` to be able to format date and number data in Sheets. 

@jennybc we talked about this a few months ago in #81,  please let me know what you think of this, even if it's just this is not the path forward for `googlesheets4`! I did try an approach to formatting using `vctrs` (https://github.com/mattle24/googlesheets4/pull/1), but I found it to be less flexible for supporting both numbers and dates, since the types are separate in R but similar in Google Sheets. Also, I think that formatting directly on the Google Sheet, rather than manipulating the R data frame, could make it easier to add more formatting (color, alignment, etc.) down the road.

Thanks for the work on the package, it's really useful!

title: remove mention of `sheets_write` still working
description:
In the man page for `sheet_write` there is still mention of `sheets_write` working despite in the version of the current master branch (0.2.0.9000) it isn't exported. 

Checking the full directory:

```bash
grep -rnw '.' -e 'sheets_write'
```
```
./vignettes/articles/function-class-names.Rmd:99:  "`sheets_write()`",            "`sheet_write()`"
./R/sheet_write.R:38:#' had `sheets_write()`. It still works, but it's deprecated and will go away
./man/sheet_write.Rd:65:had \code{sheets_write()}. It still works, but it's deprecated and will go away
```

I've deleted the sentence "It still works, but it's deprecated and will go away" but maybe we should point to the vignette [here](https://googlesheets4.tidyverse.org/articles/articles/function-class-names.html#previous-use-of-sheets_-prefix) or something as well for extra clarity.

Thank you!

title: Quick-and-dirty CSV reading via sheets_speedread
description:
Closes #122 

In #122, OP shared a public Sheet that takes 190s to read via `sheets_read()`, which uses the richest API endpoint to access data. I still think for small Sheets, this is the way to go. But I should also expose a function that reads via CSV.

This Sheet holds 56768 rows x 25 columns of NBA data, around 1.5 million cells. I consider this a very large Sheet.

In this PR I wrap up some quick-and-dirty CSV-based reading methods that are much faster, albeit more inconsistent / less featured than `sheets_read()`. For the same example Sheet, read times are about 40x faster.

```
> bnch
# A tibble: 4 x 13
  expression                                                     min median
  <bch:expr>                                                   <bch> <bch:>
1 sheets_speedread(ss, .url = "export", .method = "vroom")     5.16s  5.47s
2 sheets_speedread(ss, .url = "export", .method = "readr")     4.18s  5.36s
3 sheets_speedread(ss, .url = "datasource", .method = "vroom") 4.48s  5.16s
4 sheets_speedread(ss, .url = "datasource", .method = "readr") 5.96s  6.34s
# … with 10 more variables: `itr/sec` <dbl>, mem_alloc <bch:byt>, `gc/sec` <dbl>,
#   n_itr <int>, n_gc <dbl>, total_time <bch:tm>, result <list>, memory <list>,
#   time <list>, gc <list>
```

title: Delete dimension
description:
Fixes #30 
To make the task of deleting columns and rows simpler for other users of googlesheets4, I wrapped this task into a function called delete_dimensions

I realize that the name delete_dimensions doesn't quite fit the current function naming taxonomy for `googlesheets4`, so I'm open to suggestions as to how this could be more appropriately named.

The function uses two internals declared above it in delete_dimensions.R. One of which is `letters_to_num2` which performs a similar function to `cellranger::letters_to_num` but accounts for character specifications of a series of columns ie `B:D` and will output two column index numbers in this case. I just wanted to point this one out due to it's similarity to `letters_to_num`.

**Of note:** I included tests in test-delete_dimensions.R which work when I test using a sheet I have access to. I modified the code in the pull request to be similar to some of the other existing tests and use `test_sheet_create` such that it *should* work when Travis CI runs those tests with the credentials for the `googlesheets4-testing` account. 

I did not include a modification in `NEWS.md` as per the contributing guidelines as I wasn't sure about the naming of the function yet. However, if you're ok with it as is, let me know and I can go ahead and do so.

I also used Roxygen `7.0.2.9000` to build the Rd files. However, running it with devtools::document changed all the manual files. However, I only committed those files pertaining to the functions in the PR. I also did not include the modification to the DESCRIPTION file that updates the RoxygenNote version at the bottom. 

delete_dimension.R:
 - add letter_to_num2 to account for series of character column index specifications ie B:D
 - add split_consecutive for splitting apart non-consecutive row or column specifications in a single call
- add delete_dimension:
 - delete specific rows or columns in a single call
 - character or numeric column specifications accepted

test-delete_dimensions.R:
 - tests row deletion, numeric column deletion and character column deletion

title: Pass .name_repair from read_sheet() to spread_sheet_impl_()
description: `read_sheet()` takes a parameter `.name_repair` to eventually pass to `tibble::as_tibble`, but this parameter is never passed to `spread_sheet_impl_()`. Thus, when calling `read_sheet()`, `.name_repair` is always set to `unique` regardless of what value is passed in the original parameter. This change passes the parameter to `spread_sheet_impl_()` so the user's setting will actually be applied.
